methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Pipedream is a Series A infrastructure and logistics company founded by Garrett McCurrach and Canon Reeves. The company has raised $22.4M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of public comparables and private peer transactions in the available dataset, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $22M total raised proxy, reflecting typical dilution and value creation expected between Series A and subsequent financing stages. This approach yields a median valuation of $45M, with a low bound of $38M and high bound of $52M. The range reflects standard variance around Series A progression assumptions, though the single-method approach introduces material dependency on the assumed multiplier.

The valuation range of $38M–$52M (median $45M) is supported by stage-typical capital deployment patterns but carries elevated uncertainty given the absence of sector-specific comparables. Key risks to this range include timing to next fundraise, burn rate relative to deployed capital, and actual traction in the infrastructure logistics vertical. Any material shift in company performance or market conditions in the sector should prompt recalibration once private transaction or public comp data emerges.
